passages.text: A Maskil of Asaph.
passages.sermon:
Asaph wrote this psalm.
Asaph was a leader and musician in Israel.
This psalm is a maskil.
A maskil is a song or poem meant to teach wisdom.

passages.text: Why have You rejected us forever, O God? Why does Your anger smolder against the sheep of Your pasture?
passages.sermon:
Asaph wrote this psalm.
Asaph was a leader among the Levites.
He spoke to God.
He asked God a question.
He said, “O God, why have You rejected us forever?”
He asked, “Why does Your anger burn against Your people?”
He called God’s people the sheep of God’s pasture.
He saw that God’s anger was strong.
He felt that God’s people were left alone.
passages.original: מַשְׂכִּ֗יל לְאָ֫סָ֥ף לָמָ֣ה אֱ֭לֹהִים זָנַ֣חְתָּ לָנֶ֑צַח יֶעְשַׁ֥ן אַ֝פְּךָ֗ בְּצֹ֣אן מַרְעִיתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Remember Your congregation, which You purchased long ago and redeemed as the tribe of Your inheritance— Mount Zion where You dwell.
passages.sermon:
Asaph wrote this psalm.
He speaks to God.
God, You have a congregation.
You purchased this congregation long ago.
You redeemed this congregation.
This congregation is the tribe of Your inheritance.
You dwell on Mount Zion.
Mount Zion is where You live.
passages.original: זְכֹ֤ר עֲדָתְךָ֨׀ קָ֘נִ֤יתָ קֶּ֗דֶם גָּ֭אַלְתָּ שֵׁ֣בֶט נַחֲלָתֶ֑ךָ הַר־ צִ֝יּ֗וֹן זֶ֤ה׀ שָׁכַ֬נְתָּ בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Turn Your steps to the everlasting ruins, to everything in the sanctuary the enemy has destroyed.
passages.sermon:
God, You are powerful and holy.
The enemy has destroyed Your sanctuary.
The enemy has left everlasting ruins.
Turn Your steps toward these ruins.
See all the destruction in Your holy place.
passages.original: הָרִ֣ימָה פְ֭עָמֶיךָ לְמַשֻּׁא֣וֹת נֶ֑צַח כָּל־ הֵרַ֖ע אוֹיֵ֣ב בַּקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃

passages.text: Your foes have roared within Your meeting place; they have unfurled their banners as signs, like men wielding axes in a thicket of trees and smashing all the carvings with hatchets and picks.
passages.sermon:
God, Your enemies have entered Your meeting place.
They have roared loudly inside it.
They have set up their banners as signs.
They have shown their power and presence.
They acted like men who swing axes in a thick forest.
They used hatchets and picks.
They smashed all the carved wood inside.
passages.original: שָׁאֲג֣וּ צֹ֭רְרֶיךָ בְּקֶ֣רֶב מוֹעֲדֶ֑ךָ שָׂ֖מוּ אוֹתֹתָ֣ם אֹתֽוֹת׃ יִ֭וָּדַע כְּמֵבִ֣יא לְמָ֑עְלָה בִּֽסֲבָךְ־ עֵ֝֗ץ קַרְדֻּמּֽוֹת׃ וְעֵת פִּתּוּחֶ֣יהָ יָּ֑חַד בְּכַשִּׁ֥יל וְ֝כֵֽילַפֹּ֗ת יַהֲלֹמֽוּן׃

passages.text: They have burned Your sanctuary to the ground; they have defiled the dwelling place of Your Name.
passages.sermon:
The enemy burned Your sanctuary with fire.
They destroyed it completely.
They defiled the place where Your Name dwells.
They made Your holy dwelling unclean.
passages.original: שִׁלְח֣וּ בָ֭אֵשׁ מִקְדָּשֶׁ֑ךָ לָ֝אָ֗רֶץ חִלְּל֥וּ מִֽשְׁכַּן־ שְׁמֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: They said in their hearts, “We will crush them completely.” They burned down every place where God met us in the land.
passages.sermon:
The enemies attacked God's people.
They decided to destroy them completely.
They made this decision in their hearts.
They burned down every meeting place of God in the land.
They destroyed all the places where God met His people.
passages.original: אָמְר֣וּ בְ֭לִבָּם נִינָ֣ם יָ֑חַד שָׂרְפ֖וּ כָל־ מוֹעֲדֵי־ אֵ֣ל בָּאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: There are no signs for us to see. There is no longer any prophet. And none of us knows how long this will last.
passages.sermon: We do not see any signs.\r\nThere is no prophet among us now.\r\nNo one with us knows how long this will continue.
passages.original: אֽוֹתֹתֵ֗ינוּ לֹ֥א רָ֫אִ֥ינוּ אֵֽין־ ע֥וֹד נָבִ֑יא וְלֹֽא־ אִ֝תָּ֗נוּ יֹדֵ֥עַ עַד־ מָֽה׃

passages.text: How long, O God, will the enemy taunt You? Will the foe revile Your name forever?
passages.sermon:
God, You are powerful and holy.
Enemies insult You.
They mock Your name.
They do this again and again.
God, how long will this continue?
Will the enemy keep taunting You forever?
Will the foe always speak against Your name?
passages.original: עַד־ מָתַ֣י אֱ֭לֹהִים יְחָ֣רֶף צָ֑ר יְנָ֘אֵ֤ץ אוֹיֵ֖ב שִׁמְךָ֣ לָנֶֽצַח׃

passages.text: Why do You withdraw Your strong right hand? Stretch it out to destroy them!
passages.sermon:
God, You have great power.
You have a strong right hand.
Why do You hold back Your power?
Why do You keep Your right hand close to Yourself?
Take out Your right hand.
Use it to destroy the enemy.
passages.original: לָ֤מָּה תָשִׁ֣יב יָ֭דְךָ וִֽימִינֶ֑ךָ מִקֶּ֖רֶב חוֹקְךָ כַלֵּֽה׃

passages.text: Yet God is my King from ancient times, working salvation on the earth.
passages.sermon: God is my King.\r\nGod has ruled from ancient times.\r\nGod works salvation on the earth.
passages.original: וֵ֭אלֹהִים מַלְכִּ֣י מִקֶּ֑דֶם פֹּעֵ֥ל יְ֝שׁוּע֗וֹת בְּקֶ֣רֶב הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: You divided the sea by Your strength; You smashed the heads of the dragons of the sea; You crushed the heads of Leviathan; You fed him to the creatures of the desert.
passages.sermon:
God is strong.
God divided the sea with His power.
God broke the heads of the sea monsters.
God crushed the heads of Leviathan.
God gave Leviathan as food to the wild creatures in the desert.
passages.original: אַתָּ֤ה פוֹרַ֣רְתָּ בְעָזְּךָ֣ יָ֑ם שִׁבַּ֖רְתָּ רָאשֵׁ֥י תַ֝נִּינִ֗ים עַל־ הַמָּֽיִם׃ אַתָּ֣ה רִ֭צַּצְתָּ רָאשֵׁ֣י לִוְיָתָ֑ן תִּתְּנֶ֥נּוּ מַ֝אֲכָ֗ל לְעָ֣ם לְצִיִּֽים׃

passages.text: You broke open the fountain and the flood; You dried up the ever-flowing rivers.
passages.sermon:
God is powerful and acts in the world.
God broke open the fountain.
God broke open the flood.
God dried up the ever-flowing rivers.
passages.original: אַתָּ֣ה בָ֭קַעְתָּ מַעְיָ֣ן וָנָ֑חַל אַתָּ֥ה ה֝וֹבַ֗שְׁתָּ נַהֲר֥וֹת אֵיתָֽן׃

passages.text: The day is Yours, and also the night; You established the moon and the sun.
passages.sermon:
God owns the day.
God owns the night.
God made the moon.
God made the sun.
passages.original: לְךָ֣ י֭וֹם אַף־ לְךָ֥ לָ֑יְלָה אַתָּ֥ה הֲ֝כִינ֗וֹתָ מָא֥וֹר וָשָֽׁמֶשׁ׃

passages.text: You set all the boundaries of the earth; You made the summer and winter.
passages.sermon: God set all the boundaries of the earth.\r\nGod made the summer.\r\nGod made the winter.
passages.original: אַתָּ֣ה הִ֭צַּבְתָּ כָּל־ גְּבוּל֣וֹת אָ֑רֶץ קַ֥יִץ וָ֝חֹ֗רֶף אַתָּ֥ה יְצַרְתָּם׃

passages.text: Remember how the enemy has mocked You, O LORD, how a foolish people has spurned Your name.
passages.sermon:
The psalmist speaks to the LORD.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The psalmist asks the LORD to remember something.
The enemy has mocked the LORD.
A foolish people has rejected the LORD’s name.
passages.original: זְכָר־ זֹ֗את א֭וֹיֵב חֵרֵ֣ף׀ יְהוָ֑ה וְעַ֥ם נָ֝בָ֗ל נִֽאֲצ֥וּ שְׁמֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Do not deliver the soul of Your dove to beasts; do not forget the lives of Your afflicted forever.
passages.sermon:
God, you care for your people.
Your people are gentle and innocent, like a dove.
Do not hand over the life of your dove to wild beasts.
Your people are poor and suffering.
Do not forget the lives of your afflicted people forever.
passages.original: אַל־ תִּתֵּ֣ן לְ֭חַיַּת נֶ֣פֶשׁ תּוֹרֶ֑ךָ חַיַּ֥ת עֲ֝נִיֶּ֗יךָ אַל־ תִּשְׁכַּ֥ח לָנֶֽצַח׃

passages.text: Consider Your covenant, for haunts of violence fill the dark places of the land.
passages.sermon:
God, You made a covenant with Your people.
Look at Your covenant now.
The land has many dark places.
Violence fills these dark places.
Evil people hide in these places.
They do violent things there.
Remember Your promise, God.
See the violence in the land.
passages.original: הַבֵּ֥ט לַבְּרִ֑ית כִּ֥י מָלְא֥וּ מַחֲשַׁכֵּי־ אֶ֝֗רֶץ נְא֣וֹת חָמָֽס׃

passages.text: Do not let the oppressed retreat in shame; may the poor and needy praise Your name.
passages.sermon:
The psalmist speaks to God.
He asks God to protect the oppressed.
He says, “Do not let the oppressed go back in shame.”
He asks God to help the poor and needy.
He says, “Let the poor and needy praise Your name.”
passages.original: אַל־ יָשֹׁ֣ב דַּ֣ךְ נִכְלָ֑ם עָנִ֥י וְ֝אֶבְי֗וֹן יְֽהַלְל֥וּ שְׁמֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Rise up, O God; defend Your cause! Remember how the fool mocks You all day long.
passages.sermon:
God, You are powerful and just.
Rise up now.
Defend Your cause.
Fools insult You all day long.
Remember their insults.
Do not forget how they mock You.
passages.original: קוּמָ֣ה אֱ֭לֹהִים רִיבָ֣ה רִיבֶ֑ךָ זְכֹ֥ר חֶרְפָּתְךָ֥ מִנִּי־ נָ֝בָ֗ל כָּל־ הַיּֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Do not disregard the clamor of Your adversaries, the uproar of Your enemies that ascends continually.
passages.sermon:
God, You have enemies.
Your adversaries make noise against You.
Their voices rise up all the time.
Do not ignore their loud clamor.
Do not forget the uproar of those who oppose You.
Their attacks continue without stopping.
passages.original: אַל־ תִּ֭שְׁכַּח ק֣וֹל צֹרְרֶ֑יךָ שְׁא֥וֹן קָ֝מֶ֗יךָ עֹלֶ֥ה תָמִֽיד׃
